text:
Jordan (AE): Hey team — Zenith POC just reported streaming failures in their web client. They see SSE disconnects and occasionally partial JSON chunks that break the parser. Can someone help triage?

Anya (Support): Saw the logs they pasted in the ticket. Client error: "Unexpected end of JSON input" while parsing event payload. Happens ~10-20% of streams, seems random. Repro rate higher when throughput spikes.

Lina (Eng): Can you paste an example of the raw SSE stream around the failure? Need to know if events are truncated mid-line or missing the terminating "\n"

Anya (Support): From their capture (sanitized):
```\ndata: {"id":"1","delta":{"content":"Hello wor"\n\ndata: {"id":"1","delta":{"content":"ld"}}\n```
Client saw first event but parser failed because the newline splitting got messed up — they only buffer until a blank line then parse, but partial chunk cut the line.

Devon (SRE): That looks like chunk reassembly issue. Are they behind a corporate proxy or using CloudFront? We had similar when upstream used buffering or re-chunked SSE responses. Which infra for customer?

Jordan (AE): Zenith runs a single-page app via their CDN (Fastly) and an internal BFF on AWS ALB + nginx. They mentioned intermittent interruptions, usually after ~30s of streaming.

Lina (Eng): ALB/CloudFront/NGINX can buffer or coalesce chunks. Two common causes: (1) proxy buffering enabled (coalesces partial SSE frames) or (2) keepalive/timeouts close the TCP connection leading to a final partial chunk delivered. We should check for any intermediate `proxy_buffering on` or missing `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` headers.

Anya (Support): I asked them to provide raw curl -N output. They sent this snippet:
```\ncurl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \ 
  https://bff.zenith.io/api/generate
```
Output shows stream lines, then suddenly stops with last line truncated.

Lina (Eng): Ask them to run curl with `--no-buffer` and `-v` to see response headers. Also check whether their nginx BFF is setting `proxy_buffering off; proxy_cache_bypass 1;` and whether it forwards `X-Accel-Buffering: no`. If Fastly is in front, they may need `Cache-Control: no-transform` or a specific config to prevent reassembly.

Devon (SRE): I'll drop the checklist to triage:
- Confirm response headers (Content-Type: text/event-stream, Transfer-Encoding: chunked, Connection: keep-alive)
- Check BFF/nginx config for `proxy_buffering` or `chunked_transfer_encoding` toggles
- Look at ALB idle timeout vs app heartbeat interval (ALB default 60s)
- Inspect network captures for `FIN`/`RST` or upstream reconnects

Jordan (AE): Customer asked about quick mitigations — they want something they can apply without deep infra changes.

Lina (Eng): Quick mitigation options:
- On client: implement tolerant parser that can reassemble partial events (buffer until full JSON is valid) and retry on parser error
- On BFF: set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_set_header X-Accel-Buffering no;` for the SSE endpoint
- On CDN: disable response transformation for that route or use a raw streaming pass-through

Anya (Support): They can do the client change fast. But we should still get them a recommended nginx snippet to try on the BFF.

Lina (Eng): Snippet to try (nginx):
```\nlocation /api/generate {\n  proxy_pass http://upstream:8080;\n  proxy_set_header Host $host;\n  proxy_buffering off;\n  proxy_cache off;\n  proxy_http_version 1.1;\n  chunked_transfer_encoding on;\n  proxy_set_header Connection "";\n  proxy_set_header X-Accel-Buffering no;\n}\n```
Note: `proxy_set_header Connection "";` ensures no `Connection: close` gets forwarded unexpectedly.

Devon (SRE): Also check the app's SSE flush cadence. If the app writes small amounts but doesn't flush, proxies might combine them. Add periodic heartbeat `:\n` or `data: \n` every 15s so intermediaries keep the connection 'active'.

Jordan (AE): Customer asked about rate limits — could our platform be closing streams due to per-connection token limits?

Anya (Support): I checked our logs for their org token — no enforced short stream closes or explicit SSE kill messages. `deploy-bot` showed no recent restarts for the model host during their failure window.

deploy-bot: Model host pool health check: all hosts reporting healthy at 2026-02-10T15:04:22Z. No service restarts in window.

Lina (Eng): Good. So likely network reassembly/buffering. Also confirm the client EventSource/Fetch implementation — some browsers buffer aggressively on mobile webviews. If they have mobile app BFF, it might be caused there.

Anya (Support): Action items for Zenith (quick wins):
1) Try client-side tolerant parser + auto-retry on parse error (easy to ship)
2) Apply nginx snippet on BFF for SSE route (low-risk config change)
3) Add short heartbeat (`:keepalive` comment or empty data) every 10-15s to prevent idle timeouts

Jordan (AE): I'll relay. If they apply nginx change, they can send us curl -N -v headers again.

Devon (SRE): If issues persist after those changes, we'll ask for tcpdump of the connection to inspect chunk boundaries. I can help analyze.

Lina (Eng): Also share this note with their infra team: if using Fastly/CloudFront, confirm streaming support is enabled and no automatic re-chunking. For Fastly, `bereq.http.Connection` and `set bereq.http.Transfer-Encoding` flags matter.

Anya (Support): OK I've posted the mitigation steps in the support ticket and asked for the curl -N -v output after nginx change. Zenith says they'll try client parser fix this afternoon and nginx change tomorrow.

Jordan (AE): Thanks all. If they want a quick patch we can provide a sample client-side reassembly snippet. I can draft it.

Lina (Eng): If you want, send the sample here and I'll sign off. Keep me posted. :thumbsup:

Jordan (AE): Will do. Closing thread for now, will reopen if they still see parse failures. :rocket:
